title: Sequential-led model-variant compare controller with adaptive rollback
creator: Priya Patel
description: Build a production-ready A/B testing controller for model versions that uses sequential hypothesis testing, adaptive exposure control, and deterministic auto-rollback hooks. This ticket defines the experiment setup UX, the exposure governor (per-customer and global budgets), the statistical checks (alpha-spending / sequential p-value adjustments), and the safety policy integration (safety signal thresholds + automated rollback). Goal: enable PMs and engineers to run short-lived canaries and multi-day A/B runs with strong false-positive controls and minimal manual oversight.
status_updates: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff with Eng (Liam) + DX (Maya) + Security (Omar). Agreed scope: controller API + Console surface + webhook for rollback.

2026-03-04 - Technical spike completed by ENG: recommended alpha-spending using Pocock-like boundary for daily analysis to balance early detection and false positives. Spike PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ab-controller/pull/43

2026-03-06 - Design review: initial Console wireframes (DES-412) show single flow for 'Canary' and 'A/B' with advanced options collapsed. Request from design: add an 'explainability' panel showing per-metric delta and confidence band.
2026-03-08 - Security flagged KMS usage for experiment logs and requirement for anonymized cohort ids for regulated customers. Marked security_review_required = true.
2026-03-10 - PM decision: default exposure schedule = 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 4 checkpoints by default; can opt into 'fast detect' 5% -> 50%.
acceptance_criteria: Controller API can create, update, and pause experiments via REST + SDK
Exposure governor supports both percent-based and token-budget-based controls (global and per-customer)
Sequential testing engine reports adjusted p-values and stopping decisions; configurable alpha spending rule
Console shows experiment health, per-metric deltas with confidence intervals, and an explainability panel
Auto-rollback webhook triggers a safe fallback to previous model and logs a rollback incident with root-cause placeholders
Safety signals (content filter breaches, hallucination regressions, high FPR) can be mapped to immediate rollback or alert-only modes
End-to-end test that runs a synthetic experiment and validates rollback triggers under simulated signal thresholds
